incident.title: InventoryError when cancelling an order after 'Buy again'

It seems to affect customers who used 'Buy again' on that order and then changed quantities in their new cart. The stack trace points into the inventory module, so we suspect the reservation bookkeeping.

payload.title: Inventory.release() mis-tracks reserved stock
payload.explanation: The exception is thrown inside Inventory.release; the reservation counter may be decremented or keyed incorrectly so a legitimate release looks like an over-release.
evidence_for: Stack trace ends in inventory.js release()
evidence_against: Only orders touched by 'Buy again' are affected

payload.title: Cart.restore() shares line items with the past order
payload.explanation: buyAgain() passes order.lines into Cart.restore, which stores the same LineItem objects. Adding 3 more mugs mutates the order's line from 2 to 5, so cancel() tries to release 5 units while only 2 are reserved.
evidence_for: Order was placed with 2 mugs, release asks for 5 = 2 + 3 added after Buy again
restore() doc comment promises the cart keeps its own copies

payload.title: Cart.restore() aliased past order line items
payload.markdown:
# Postmortem: Cart.restore() aliased past order line items

## Summary
Cancelling an order failed with InventoryError after the customer used 'Buy again' and changed quantities, because the new cart shared LineItem objects with the old order.

## Impact
Support could not cancel affected orders; reserved stock stayed locked and the order record showed quantities the customer never bought.

## Root cause
Cart.restore() stored the order's LineItem objects directly. Cart.add() mutates line.quantity in place, so editing the new cart rewrote the past order (2 -> 5 mugs). Inventory.release() then correctly refused to release 5 units with only 2 reserved.

## Evidence
- Hypothesis 'Inventory.release() mis-tracks reserved stock' was disproven: reserve/release bookkeeping tests pass
- Reproduction test showed order.lines[0].quantity === 5 after adding 3 to the new cart
- Commit "feat: 'Buy again' on past orders" introduced restore()
- Ruled out: _Inventory.release() mis-tracks reserved stock_ — reproduction test passed (2 passed): the predicted defect is absent

## Fix
restore() now stores item.copy() for each saved line, matching its documented contract.

## How it was verified
Both reproduction tests pass; the existing suite is unchanged and green.

- Reproduction test `tests/fixsi/buy-again-does-not-mutate-order.test.js` failed before the fix and passes after it.
- Full suite: 32 passed, 0 failed (baseline: 30 passed). Pre-existing tests were not modified.
- Fix attempts: 1.

## Prevention
- Make LineItem immutable (Object.freeze) and return new objects on change
- Test that APIs documented as 'copies' are not aliasing their inputs

---
